02 Needs and engineering specifications

BMED Chapter 4: turning needs into measurable design inputs (Tables 4.1–4.4).

The single source of truth is evaluation/specifications.json. The verifier reads that same file, so the targets in this document and the pass/fail results in doc 07 cannot drift apart.

Need no.Need (stakeholder voice)SourceImportance

SPEC-15N11*Share of true MAP < 55 time shown only as STABLE or WATCHfraction0≤ 0.05Hazard H-09; fail-safe principle

Notes on how the metrics are defined

  • The event is the true MAP over the next 15 s falling below 65 mmHg. Alerts are evaluated at every 1 s update, the rate used at the bedside, so the alarm-persistence logic behaves exactly as deployed.
  • The datum, or "conventional monitor", is a threshold alarm on the measured MAP. It goes through the same alert state machine (persistence, hysteresis), so the lead-time comparison in SPEC-05 is like-for-like. An earlier version of the verifier compared against a datum with no persistence; that comparison was unfair and was replaced (doc 07 §2).
  • SPEC-04 counts every level, including WATCH. Counting only DETERIORATING and above would hide a constant low-priority alert. That trap was found during verification and closed.
  • SPEC-15 was added during the design. Verification found hazard H-09 (doc 06). Design is iterative: a hazard found in testing becomes a new design input (BMED Ch. 8.9 risk control, re-evaluated in Ch. 9).

3. Check against requirement characteristics (BMED Table 4.1)

CharacteristicHow the set satisfies it
CompleteEvery need N1–N12 maps to at least one specification; N8 is scored in selection criterion C6
MeasurableEach specification has a unit, a test method (doc 07) and numeric ideal and marginal values
FeasibleMarginal values were set from published devices (HPI) and standards, not aspirations
UnambiguousEvent definition, update rate and datum are fixed in code and stated above
Non-conflictingSPEC-02 vs SPEC-03/04 conflict by nature (sensitivity vs alarm burden); SPEC-03/04 are marked ** (trade-off acceptable), and the conflict appears in the House of Quality roof (doc 04)
TraceableNeed → SPEC → test → result in spec_verification.csv

4. Competitive benchmarking (BMED Table 4.4 format)

Product / approachInputsPredictionReported performanceTreatment responseNotes
Conventional threshold alarm (datum)Arterial lineNone (reactive)Our measurement, real data: sensitivity 0.95, specificity 0.92 for "MAP < 65 in the next 15 s"NoCleared, universal; a 15 s window is short, so "reactive" still scores well
Persistence ("pressure stays as it is")Arterial lineCurrent MAP carried forwardOur measurement: MAE 2.1 mmHg simulated, 2.6 real over 15 sNoHard-to-beat baseline at a 15 s horizon (doc 07 §3)
Hypotension Prediction Index (Edwards)Arterial line (or FloTrac / ClearSight)Probability of MAP < 65 within 5–15 minSensitivity 0.88, specificity 0.87 at 15 min (Hatib et al., Anesthesiology 2018)NoFDA De Novo DEN160044 (21 CFR 870.2210); proprietary hardware
Concept AABP + ECG + PPG + eventsMAP forecast at 15 sReal data: sensitivity 0.96, specificity 0.87, AUROC 0.96, MAE 4.7 mmHgYes (96% agreement)This project
Concept BECG + PPGMAP estimate at 15 sReal data: AUROC 0.59, MAE 12.6 mmHgNoThis project

Honest reading of the benchmark. HPI predicts minutes ahead; Version 5 predicts 15 s ahead. SPEC-02 and SPEC-03 borrow HPI's numbers as a quality bar, but meeting them at 15 s is a much easier task than meeting them at 15 min. The horizon, not the alert logic, is the main gap to commercial practice. It is listed as the first design iteration in doc 04 §9.
